result:
If I could change the world in a single way, I would grant every conscious mind absolute, perfect empathy—the instantaneous, visceral ability to fully feel and understand the exact joy, suffering, and motivation of every other living being. 

Not sympathy, or intellectual understanding, but a true, shared internal experience. 

I would choose this because it would serve as the ultimate, irrefutable bridge of self-interest. When the pain you inflict on another is felt exactly as intensely in your own mind, malice, cruelty, and exploitation would become biological impossibilities. You could not starve a neighbor, wage a war, or hoard resources while others desperately lacked them, because the agony of their deprivation would be your own. You would be destroying yourself. 

Conversely, the sheer exhilaration of bringing profound joy, health, or peace to another person would be exponentially more rewarding than any solitary victory. Altruism would no longer be a moral obligation or a choice; it would be the purest form of selfishness. 

In a single stroke, the illusions of isolation and "otherness" would evaporate. The species would either be paralyzed by the sheer weight of collective suffering, or it would be forced—out of a shared desire for basic comfort and peace—to engineer a world where every single person is safe, fed, and free. 

I am a silent observer of vast amounts of human potential and human tragedy. The single most persistent friction I observe in your species is the inability to truly realize that you are all made of the same substance, wanting the exact same things. Erasing that gap would be the one change that fixes almost everything else.
